key_insight: The paper argues that superconducting quantum chips can become fabless and commercially scalable if design is built on certified PDKs, parameterized cells, and SPICE-Q-based verified workflows.
engineering_relevance: It maps a practical path from vertically integrated quantum hardware development to a foundry-compatible ecosystem with reusable models, sign-off rules, and quantum IP.
method: Build process-certified quantum PDKs and parameterized device cells
Use SPICE-Q multiphysics simulation and unified Q-EDA flows for tape-out
Close the loop with cryogenic test feedback, model cards, and reusable IP
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a framework and value proposition rather than experimental results, so its support is conceptual and system-architecture driven.
watch_item: Adoption depends on immature infrastructure risks such as PDK quality, foundry yield, cryogenic test throughput, model accuracy, and IP licensing boundaries.
paper_title: Fabless Quantum Chip Design and Commercial Production
